key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the complaint alleged suppression of the fact that FCIL had been referred to the BIFR and was likely to be declared a sick company, which allegedly induced IEL to pay a sum to BCCL in return for ammonium nitrate.
witness_credibility: The court assessed that the complainant was aware of FCIL's financial health at the time of entering into the agreement, and the allegations in the complaint did not establish the necessary dishonest intention at the time of the agreement.

legal_representation.accused: Jaideep Gupta, Shweta Bharti, Ahanthem Henry, Saurabh Raj Sinha, Ghanshyam Joshi, Oipak Kumar Jena, Sanjoy Ghosh, Avijit Bhattacharjee

investigation_status: Complaint filed, summons issued, petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 filed and dismissed by High Court

appeal_history.supreme_court: Supreme Court allowed the appeals, set aside the High Court's order and quashed the magistrate's order

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellants had dishonestly induced the complainant company to enter into a tripartite agreement, suppressing the fact that FCIL was likely to be declared a sick company, thereby causing the complainant to pay a large sum of money to BCCL in return for ammonium nitrate which was not supplied.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the complaint lacked the basic ingredients of the offences under Sections 420, 406, and 1208 of the IPC, as there was no evidence of fraudulent intention at the time of entering into the agreement, and the complainant was aware of FCIL's financial health.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that to establish cheating under Section 415 IPC, there must be a fraudulent or dishonest intention at the time of making the promise, which cannot be presumed merely from failure to keep the promise subsequently.
precedent_relied_upon: Ram Jas vs. State of UP (1970) 2 SCC 740; Hridaya Ranjan Prasad Verma and Ors. vs. State of Bihar and Anr. (2000) 4 SCC 168; Anil Mahajan vs. Bhor Industries Ltd. and Anr. (2005) 10 C sec 228; Onkar Nath Mishra and Ors. vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and Anr. (2008) 2 SCC 561; Common Cause, A Registered Society vs. Union of India and Ors. (1999) 6 SCC 667
